says: In next/, since T502 S2 no product code builds a Process service with `processRuntime`: the object builds `processLayer` through `ObjectService.make` with the app's checked read, while seven test files (readers.laws, alarm.laws A1, error-cause, IsolateUsage, checklist-instance.laws, runtime-recovery.laws) still drive `processRuntime`, which reads the setting by the library's own path and skips `settingsWire`.
proof: `rg -n "processRuntime|processLayer" next -g '*.ts'` at this head lists `processRuntime` only at runtime.ts:1615-1616 and in those seven .test.ts files; the one product user of a Process service is ProcessObject.ts:74, which calls `processLayer`. `pnpm lint:dead` does not flag it, because test files count as users.
cost: The recovery and reader laws keep driving a composition the instance no longer runs, so a change to how the object builds its service (the checked read, settingsWire's failure shape) can pass them unseen; the export stays only for tests.
